mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months compresses the risk-free rate, reducing the discount rate applied to future equity cash flows and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered instances, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 1.5% for three consecutive months, it signals a tightening monetary policy that increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate profitability, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered instances, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate and an increase in non-farm payrolls signals strong labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered instances, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of late-cycle expansion periods, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered instances, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.
